newsitem.title: USA: Hershey says net income cut by sale of European units.
newsitem.headline: Hershey says net income cut by sale of European units.

text.p: Chocolate maker Hershey Foods Corp. Tuesday reported record sales for the fourth quarter, but its earnings fell due to the sale of two overseas businesses.

The Hershey, Pa.-based maker of candy and grocery products said its earnings fell to $78.7 million, or 51 cents a share, in the latest quarter, reflecting the sale of chocolate and confectionary makers in Europe, which cut its earnings by $35.3 million. Sales were a record $1.18 billion.
In the 1995 fourth quarter, it earned $105.8 million, or 68 cents a share, on sales of $1.11 billion.
For the 1996 year, the company posted earnings of $273.1 million or $1.77 a share vs. 1995 earnings of $282.0 million or $1.70 a share. Sales increased to $4.0 billion from $3.7 billion.
"We had an excellent year in 1996, and our business enters 1997 on solid footing," said Chairman Kenneth Wolfe.
"Hershey Chocolate North America was the principal contributor to income growth for the year with important contributions also made by Hershey Grocery and Hershey International," he said.
Hershey's stock was up $1.125 at $44.75 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon.
